description: Pipeline plugin hooks. Every command routes through `hooks/run-hook.sh`, which resolves an absolute `pipeline` binary (PATH → $BUN_INSTALL/bin → ~/.bun/bin → /opt/homebrew/bin → /usr/local/bin) and runs `pipeline hook <name>` with stdin/stdout/stderr inherited — Claude Code runs hooks through a non-interactive /bin/sh that never sources ~/.zshrc, so a Dock- or Start-menu-launched session cannot otherwise see a global install. EVERY COMMAND HOOK BELOW PINS THE SHELL: `"shell": "bash"` sits beside `"type"` and `"command"` on all TEN of them (Stop 2, SubagentStop 2, SessionStart 2, PreToolUse 1, PostToolUse 1, UserPromptSubmit 1, Notification 1), and the pin is load-bearing rather than cosmetic (T-CLI-2 remedy, ROADMAP row B.5). Omitted, Claude Code picks Git Bash on Windows and FALLS BACK TO POWERSHELL when Git Bash is not installed — which hands this POSIX-sh shim to a shell that cannot execute it. That fallback was measured (T-CLI-2 / v1, PR #122) as either a hang or, worse, a dispatcher that exits 0 WITHOUT running the shim at all, which on PreToolUse turns a deny-hook into a permit: a security control that FAILS OPEN. Pinning to `bash` makes Git Bash a hard Windows prerequisite — Git for Windows (https://git-scm.com/download/win) bundles it, or `winget install --id Git.Git -e --source winget`, and README's Install section states this as the third prerequisite. Without it the hooks FAIL VISIBLY instead of silently doing nothing, and that is the intended trade — but visibility is ALL it buys, and THE PIN DOES NOT MAKE THE CONTROL FAIL CLOSED. Verified against the installed Claude Code dispatcher: a bash-pinned hook on a Windows machine with no detected Git Bash throws BEFORE the spawn, outside the spawn's own try, and the hook runner classifies that as outcome `non_blocking_error` (surfaced as `hook_non_blocking_error`, deduped per event+command per session, so about ten messages and then silence). THE TOOL CALL STILL PROCEEDS. The only path that yields outcome `blocking` is a hook that actually RAN and exited 2. So a bash-pinned PreToolUse deny-hook on a Git-Bash-less Windows box still reads as an ALLOW — an announced one, rather than one indistinguishable from a hook that ran and approved. Do not build a genuinely blocking PreToolUse hook on top of this file expecting the platform to hold it closed; it will not. macOS and Linux are unaffected. Add a new command hook and it must carry the pin too — miss one and that single event keeps the fail-open path while every other event looks fixed. A PowerShell twin of `run-hook.sh` was considered and REJECTED by the owner (2026-08-19): a second shim is a permanent drift surface, and one shell plus an honest prerequisite is the cheaper contract. The shim also absorbs VERSION SKEW: a CLI too old to know the `hook` subcommand refuses it with exit 2, which on PreToolUse would block the tool call, so the shim classifies a non-zero exit with a read-only `pipeline hook --help` probe and exits 0 (one actionable upgrade line under --loud) only when the subcommand is genuinely absent; a relay that ran and failed still propagates its exit code. THE RELAYS ARE CLI SUBCOMMANDS, NOT FILES IN THIS PLUGIN (plugin-thin p6): they live in `IvanMurzak/pipeline` as `src/hooks/*.ts`, so a hook's version is the installed CLI's version by construction. This plugin therefore REQUIRES `@baizor/pipeline` — `bun add -g @baizor/pipeline` — and the --loud SessionStart entry below is what says so when it is missing. Registrations: Stop → analytics relay (token usage from transcript) then stats relay (token + tool-failure enrichment for .pipeline/.stats/); SubagentStop (matcher: pipeline-manager) → analytics relay (manager.stopped liveness signal when a pipeline-manager subagent ends — the matcher keeps the hook from spawning for every other subagent) then stats relay; Notification → analytics relay (run.awaiting_input when a permission prompt or an input request blocks the session); SessionStart → the session relay (appends one session.opened line to the project's .runtime/events.jsonl and nothing else — this is what is left of the deleted local dashboard's launcher hook, kept because the journal is ux-v2's telemetry source and `pipeline logs` renders the event), THEN the department notifier relay (department-mesh task a1: ensures the `pipeline department notify` background daemon is running detached and drains its pending-notification journal into SessionStart additionalContext — a department task that reaches INPUT_REQUIRED/AUTH_REQUIRED or a terminal state announces itself even across sessions, gated by its own switch PIPELINE_DEPARTMENT_NOTIFY_ENABLED (falling back to the deprecated PIPELINE_MESH_NOTIFY_ENABLED with a warning), default ON, no-op until `pipeline cloud connect` has been run once); PreToolUse → analytics relay (live mirror binding + run-level bypass START synthesis for pipeline-manager spawns); PostToolUse → analytics relay (tool counts + agent spawns + bypass END/fallback lifecycle synthesis); UserPromptSubmit → prompt match relay (BM25-matches the submitted prompt against the project's PIPELINE.md manifests and, on a confident single match only, injects one line of additionalContext suggesting the pipeline — gated by its own opt-in switch PIPELINE_PROMPT_MATCH_ENABLED, off by default). The whole journal/analytics system is ON BY DEFAULT — every journal hook runs at entry unless PIPELINE_JOURNAL_ENABLED is explicitly opted out with a falsy value 0/false/no/off (the master opt-OUT switch; the prompt match relay is a separate OPT-IN gated by PIPELINE_PROMPT_MATCH_ENABLED instead, off by default) — and is additionally a no-op when cwd has no .pipeline/ (the department notifier relay is independent of this project-scoped gate — department tasks are org-scoped, not project-scoped, so it runs the same in every directory, gated only by PIPELINE_DEPARTMENT_NOTIFY_ENABLED). EXCEPTION: Stop and SubagentStop additionally run the stats relay (token + tool-failure enrichment for the per-run measurement files under .pipeline/.stats/, via the shared backfillProject core), which is ON BY DEFAULT and gated by its own PIPELINE_STATS_ENABLED (set 0 to disable); it too no-ops when the project has no .stats dir. SECOND EXCEPTION: the Notification branch is evaluated BEFORE the PIPELINE_JOURNAL_ENABLED opt-out and carries its own gate PIPELINE_AWAITING_INPUT_ENABLED (default ON, set 0 to disable) — a blocked run is worth surfacing through `pipeline logs` even for a user who is not connected to the cloud dashboard. PER-HOOK TIMEOUTS: every command hook below carries an explicit `timeout`, in SECONDS, sitting beside `type`/`command`/`shell`. Until now none did, so every hook inherited Claude Code's default — 600s (TEN MINUTES) on every event registered here except `UserPromptSubmit`, which defaults to 30s. A wedged relay could therefore hold a turn for ten minutes, and nothing in this plugin bounded it; `run-hook.sh` says so itself, in as many words: "If that ever needs closing properly, the lever is `hooks.json`'s per-hook `timeout` field, not shell code here." This is that lever. On expiry Claude Code CANCELS the hook and DISCARDS its output entirely, so the hook produces no decision at all; a `PreToolUse` timeout therefore does NOT block the tool, which proceeds through the normal permission flow (one more reason not to build a genuinely blocking PreToolUse hook on this file — see above). Hooks for one event run in parallel, each with its own timeout. THE VALUES ARE MEASURED, NOT INTUITED. Measured on a Windows 11 box with the CLI at ~/.bun/bin, driving the real shim: every relay costs 150-380ms warm and idle; a COLD first invocation of a session adds the once-per-session `pipeline --version` spawn (~120ms on its own) for 520-980ms total; and the figure that actually sets the budget is ONE hook invocation while the machine is under a heavy parallel-subagent wave, which is when a dev box is slowest — 4.1s at 8-way concurrency, 7.7s at 32-way. THE BUDGET IS A PROCESS-SPAWN BUDGET, because the relays' own work is nearly invisible beside the spawn: a 2KB, a 16MB and a 181MB transcript all timed identically, 200 pipeline manifests cost the prompt matcher no more than one did, and the department notifier's daemon spawn is DETACHED, so the path that ensures the daemon is running costs what the path that skips it costs (354-1149ms either way; its 3.3s at 16-way concurrency is spawn contention, not daemon work). That is why the values below are near-uniform rather than tuned per relay — the measurements do not support finer distinctions than the three drawn here. 20s is the floor, on the seven spawn-dominated entries (SessionStart ×2, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Notification, UserPromptSubmit): about 2.6× the measured 7.7s worst case, so a machine two-and-a-half times slower than that one under the same extreme concurrency is still never cut off, while a wedged relay costs a visible pause instead of a lost turn. 30s goes to the three transcript-folding entries (Stop's analytics AND stats relays, SubagentStop's analytics relay); their extra headroom guards an UNMEASURED path, and that gap is stated rather than hidden — no harness could provoke the transcript fold, so its true cost is unknown here, though stats-relay's Stop rung is already bounded from the inside by its own 4s STOP_BUDGET_MS. 45s, the largest value in this file, goes to exactly ONE entry: SubagentStop's stats relay, the only path the CLI's own source declares UNBUDGETED, because it folds a pipeline-manager transcript that can span an hours-long run. CANCELLATION IS SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION on all ten: every relay is best-effort telemetry, a cancelled fold simply leaves the record null for a later stop to fill, and not one of them is a blocking control — which is why generous-but-finite beats a ten-minute default in both directions. `UserPromptSubmit` is the one entry whose cap was LOWERED rather than introduced: it already defaulted to 30s, it holds the user's prompt for as long as it runs, and it measured under 1s even with 200 manifests, so 20s tightens it while still leaving more than 20× headroom. Add a new command hook and it MUST carry a timeout too — `tests/hook-run-shim.test.ts` fails CI when any entry omits one or sets one outside 5-60s, exactly as it guards the bash pin, so this paragraph cannot silently drift out of agreement with the file.
